notes.title: Alpha 0.18
notes.notes: [h1]2025-07-30 Alpha 0.18[/h1][p]After this quite long time without an update rest assured that there has been a lot of conceptual work done in the background. So many ideas, and so little time...[/p][list][*][p]Changed the sound attenuation so that the explosion of fixed targets sounds more natural[/p][/*][*][p]Implemented the client-2-server-2-clients communication for the different game modes[/p][/*][*][p]Added a message queue to display server messages to the player[/p][/*][*][p]Made the server realize when player destroy fixed targets (to count the achieved goals)[/p][/*][*][p]Learned that "Bf 109" has to be written with lowercase "f" for historical reasons.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed some colliders[/p][/*][*][p]Had a lot of ideas[/p][/*][*][p]Fought an intense battle against the urge to overscope. Again. It's a tough opponent.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed the radio in the kitchen now playing music - and added some sound attenuation[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed the collider of the toaster in the kitchen. Would be a shame if somebody would avoid a crash![/p][/*][*][p]Removed the main menu scene (to make room for another idea I have in mind)[/p][/*][*][p]Vastly reduced the file size of the shipped game[/p][/*][*][p]Added some **really simple** water to the bathtub. No caustics, no ripples, no physics (yet)[/p][/*][*][p]Got distracted by my cat that insisted on sitting on my hands while I try to write code[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue with the Bf 109's landing gear that made the aircraft tip over while taking off[/p][/*][*][p]Lost nearly two entire days figuring out why the shipping build keeps crashing when compiling for DX12[/p][/*][*][p]Reverted to "Development build", which results in much greater file size, but allows for DX12 support[/p][/*][*][p]Added a fairly simple dialogue to select between a few available missions[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue that sometimes made the elevators' steering angle overflow[/p][/*][*][p]Learned about a better way to do screen capturing for video footage[/p][/*][*][p]Got side tracked [/p][/*][/list]

[/p][p][/p][h1]2025-04-29 Some relesenotes discontinuity[/h1][p]We have had a major set-back due to my evident lack of ability to assess the importance of getting the games architecture right before building content. Long story short: The initial plan was to get the game loop running, test out wether it is fun to play, and if so, add multiplayer support.[/p][p]Well... turns out that in Unreal Engine, multiplayer is not a feature, but a fundamental design decission. I ought to have known that, given all the years of programming. But somehow I managed to ignore this fact. After several weeks (honestly it have been months) of trying to get it working, I ditched all implementation an started a completely empty project - and rebuilt the game from scratch.[/p][p]There were some versions I put on Steam, but in a different branch, to be ablte to test some multiplayer stuff, server synchronisation, motion prediction, replication - all that stuff you don't want to know about while playing, but that has to be done right in order to make the game work as intended. Those versions (Alpha 0.7 - Alpha 0.9) are nothing you should waste your time with, so I didn't make them publically available.[/p][p]But now Alpha 0.10 is around the corner. Still **a lot** of work to be done, but we are at least nearly there where we left off with Alpha 0.4.[/p][p]Have fun exploring. More things to come soon.[/p][p][/p][h1]2025-02-08 Alpha 0.6 Multiplayer [/h1][p]A lot of bug hunting. And by "a lot", I mean... well... a lot.[/p][p]On an unrelated sidenote: If the UNREAL documentation says "download and install the latest Steamworks SDK", they do not really want you to install the latest Steamworks SDK. They want you to download and install the latest Steamworks SDK **they themselves used** for the latest Unreal Engine. A small detail that cost me about 10 days of troubleshooting before realizing that the error was not on my end. At least I learned a lot along the way.[/p][p]And then I decided to start implementing a nice little feature known as "multiplayer". Turns out multiplayer is not a feature, but a design concept. I **should** have known that already, but for some reason I didn't act like I knew it. Long story short: I spent 4 months (in words: FOUR MONTHS) learning about[/p][list][*][p]the concepts of multiplayer in Unreal Engine[/p][/*][*][p]how to implement them[/p][/*][*][p]what I did wrong in my initial implementation[/p][/*][*][p]that I should start over from scratch[/p][/*][*][p]that I do know **nothing** compared to what I should know[/p][/*][/list][p]After a long time with many test-prototype-just-to-see-what-happens-experiments I started a completely new, empty project and began implementing Toybox Aces from scratch. That's why you didn't her from me for a while.[/p][p]So what did I do:[/p][list][*][p]Threw away the complete game (except the design elements like models, textures, sounds, ...)[/p][/*][*][p]Build a brand new game with empty game loop[/p][/*][*][p]Added a rudimentary main menu (basically a start button)[/p][/*][*][p]Added the test level "Kids Room 1"[/p][/*][*][p]Rebuild the Test-Aircraft to work with multiplayer physics[/p][/*][*][p]Messed up badly regarding movement prediction and client-server-communication[/p][/*][/list][h1]2025-01-11 Alpha 0.5[/h1][p]Just a quick upload of features I partly built in December, but didn't put them into the Alpha release until now.[/p][list][*][p]Played around with lobbies, invitations, Steam SDK and NetCode[/p][/*][*][p]Added first dialogues for managing the multiplayer matchmaking. Still inoperabel.[/p][/*][*][p]Added Support for PS4-Controllers (currently only tested with Dualshock USB)[/p][/*][/list][p]A long, winding road before our feet.[/p][p][/p][h1]2025-01-07 Alpha 0.4[/h1][list][*][p]Fixed the mesh of the spinning propeller[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed the sound atteunation of the engine sound so distant objects sound less loud[/p][/*][*][p]Tweaked the flight dynamics. Still some work to do with the glide dynamics[/p][/*][*][p]Added some... functionality... to the 20 mm cannons. Still no impact, but working on that.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed the version string in the main menu to reflect the dev branch[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h1]2025-01-04 Alpha 0.3[/h1][p]Did some minor changes during the last days, but no real progress.[/p][list][*][p]Started to add visuals for the propeller (both slow and fast moving). Still work in progress[/p][/*][*][p]Added glas panes for the windows. Currently installed in one window only.[/p][/*][*][p]Optimized some shaders to increase performance[/p][/*][*][p]Increased the engine power of the plane by 50%. At least for now.[/p][/*][*][p]Played with different colors[/p][/*][*][p]Added some decorative elements... like a closed cloud cover[/p][/*][*][p]Played the game way more than did actual development[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h1]2025-01-01 Alpha 0.2[/h1][p]Multiplayer! Well... at least the first steps towards multiplayer.[/p][list][*][p]Played around with multiplayer support. Oh dear, we are faaaar from a finished game[/p][/*][*][p]Added some more aircraft color variants[/p][/*][*][p]Added access to Steam friends avatar pictures (just to make the menu look a bit nicer)[/p][/*][*][p]Got the Unreal Engine NetCode to run with Toybox Aces.[/p][/*][*][p]Flew around the kids room - with multiple planes simultaniously.[/p][/*][*][p]Added some really simple main menu[/p][/*][*][p]Added a really simple logo for the main menu[/p][/*][*][p]Implemented some functionality to obtain the Steam friends list (for multiplayer invitations)[/p][/*][/list][h1]2024-12-28 Alpha 0.1[/h1][p]Today the first Alpha build hit the Steam repository. It is only visible for a small group of testers.[/p][p]No, we are not using the SteamSubsystem or stuff like that. It is the bare metal SteamSDK. A lot of hazzle to get it running at first, but then the possibilities are... well... it gets a lot of done.[/p][list][*][p]Integrated the game into the SteamSDK[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h1]What happened before Alpha 0.1[/h1][h2]2024-12-27[/h2][p]- Played around with clouds and cloud covers. May be there will be some... weather... in the kids room[/p][p]- Changed the input system to enable user defined input devices (like controllers / joysticks / ...)[/p][p]- Did some geometry celanup to avoid overlapping geometry and unnecessary triangles[/p][p]- Again had to look up which consonants in "unnecessary" have to be doubled and which not[/p][p] [/p][h2]2024-12-26 [/h2][p]- Added an artificial horizon instrumentation[/p][p]- Wasted several hours searching a bug, only to discover that in one formula I confused pitch and yaw[/p][p] [/p][h2]2024-12-25[/h2][p]- Fixed an error in the avionics formulae. Now the aircraft can properly glide without engine[/p][p]- Realized that the project wasn't fully integrated into version control. Fixed that.[/p][p]- Ate way too much[/p][p][/p][h2]2024-12-23[/h2][p]- Separated level structure (walls, floor, ...) from furniture and decorative elements[/p][p]- Added some toy cars[/p][p][/p][h2]2024-12-22[/h2][p]- Added the toy train and some decorative elements[/p][p]- Added those little plastic bricks most of us know from those Danish toy brand[/p][p]- Made the first attempt of adding some weapons to the aircraft[/p][p]- Added clouds! The are a bit costly in terms of performance, but... hey, we now have clouds.[/p][p]- Made the kids room a bit smaller to make it feel more cluttered[/p][p]- Made the camera perspective fixed to the airplane to avoid motion sicknes[/p][p]- Flew around in the kids room way more time than I'd like to admit[/p][p] [/p][h2]2024-12-20[/h2][p]- Nearly got scammed by some Nigerians. Damn, they are getting better every day! Stay sharp.[/p][p]- Implemented some basic HUD (ugly as heck, but hey, this is a prototype)[/p][p]- Implemented the rudder as working control surface. Now you can strave and slipland, if you want to[/p][p]- Experimented with different camera perspectives to optimize the follow mode[/p][p]- Got motion sick while playing with a wobbly follow cam on a huge monitor. Not recommended.[/p][p]- Added engine sound and made its volume and pitch depend on the airspeed and throttle.[/p][p] [/p][h2]Early stage: 2024-12-19[/h2][p]Took some time to set up the new project and wrap my head around what it should be like.[/p][p]But now it is here. Say hello to "Toybox Aces" - an action loaded 3D-multiplayer-air-combat-simulation with tiny toy planes, wreaking havoc all over the kids room.[/p][p]Get ready to see furniture from a different perspective![/p][p]As you may have guessed after playing Gravity Force, this game is heavily physics driven, too.[/p][p]So don't expect the aircrafts to be controlled "arcade style". They do obey to the laws of physics, and are driven by forces like thrust, drag, lift and whatever the control surfaces (aileron, rudder, elevator, ...) may produce. So you might need some time to become a flying ace. Or even a decent pilot. Or someone who doesn't crash immediately. But you will get there. Promissed.[/p][p]The project just started, so don't expect to see too much yet. But we do have plans. And planes, too.[/p][p]- Set up the project[/p][p]- Did some conceptual stuff. A lot.[/p][p]- Did some planning stuff[/p][p]- Thought about ways to downscale the physics to make it look and feel right[/p][p]- Built a first prototype as proof of concept for the physics model[/p][p]- Built a first test airplane[/p][p]- Built a simple room as test arena[/p][p]- Tried to figure out why the plane does not behave like it should[/p][p]- Narrowed the root cause of the weird behavior down to the implementation of the elevator[/p][p]- Tried to fix the elevator[/p][p]- Got mad and deleted a huge chunk of clunky, messy code that was meant to do the physics simulation[/p][p]- Got even angrier, put the game aside for a while and went for a walk.[/p][p]- Suddenly realized that the calculation for the elvator was absolutely fine, and the error was in a totally different place[/p][p]- Fixed that error within 5 minutes[/p][p]- Restored the deleted code, and looked in awe at a perfectly flying miniature airplane[/p][p]- Went to bed, knowing that tomorrow will be a day with new things to be completely messed up[/p][p][/p]
